sketches.title: Ringmaster Rebuttal
sketches.premise: You and your rival run a circus where every act must shut down the act before it. Put a new act in the ring, explain how it stops the last one, and keep the show moving until someone offers a stunt that folds faster than a cheap tent.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new standing act directly blocks, cancels, traps, exposes, or safely ends the previous act; dodging it, merely surviving it, using a bigger copy, or naming a cousin from the same act family does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one present-tense circus act and its clear counter: "I am the net, catching the flying trapeze before it reaches the other bar."
sketches.first_card: I am the cannon, firing a clown across the ring.

sketches.title: Prop Panic
sketches.premise: The circus prop table is cursed: each turn, your prop must make the prop just used useless. You are not describing a trick or escaping danger; you are putting one ordinary circus object to work against the object on the floor, while the host calmly watches the equipment budget die.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts only a concrete prop that physically removes, jams, breaks, hides, or controls the previous prop’s function; fleeing, enduring, enlarging it, or offering a related prop that does not act on it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one prop and one immediate use against the last prop: "I am the bucket, smothering the fire baton under wet sand."
sketches.first_card: I am the whip, cracking through the paper target.

sketches.title: Clown Court
sketches.premise: Two clowns argue cases in a circus court, and every new claim must defeat the last claim with a plain piece of evidence. Facts, objects, witnesses, and rules are allowed; hand-waving is not, because even a clown can spot a bad argument when it is wearing enormous shoes.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new standing claim directly proves, disproves, exposes, or legally blocks the previous claim; changing the subject, merely denying it, repeating it louder, or using a vague metaphor loses.
sketches.move_shape: State one claim and the evidence that defeats the last claim: "The cannon is safe, because the inspector’s cracked barrel is proof it must be retired."
sketches.first_card: The ringmaster claims the tightrope is safe.

sketches.title: Under the Big Top
sketches.premise: You are designing a circus safety plan one hazard at a time. Each turn adds a standing safety measure that neutralizes the danger just named before it, but a measure that only avoids the danger or hopes it misses earns the host’s driest applause.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts a measure that directly prevents, stops, contains, or makes harmless the previous circus hazard; surviving it, stepping aside, using a stronger version of the same hazard, or offering a related precaution that does not counter it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one safety measure and its direct effect: "I am the padded landing mat, stopping the falling acrobat from hitting the hard floor."
sketches.first_card: The tightrope is stretched above a concrete floor.

sketches.title: Act Breaker
sketches.premise: Each player invents a circus act, but the next player must book an act that ruins its special trick. A good counter changes what can happen in the ring; a lazy one merely stands somewhere else and hopes the audience gets distracted.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new act directly prevents, interrupts, reveals, or outperforms the previous act’s defining trick without being a bigger version of it, a same-family copy, or a mere dodge or survival tactic.
sketches.move_shape: Name an act and the trick it defeats: "I am the spotlight operator, flooding the magician’s hidden hand with light."
sketches.first_card: I am the escape artist, locked inside a steel box.

sketches.title: Tent-Town Takeover
sketches.premise: Build a tiny circus town by placing one working place after another, with each new place taking control of the last one’s job. The bakery can feed the hungry, the jail can stop the thief, and the water tower can ruin the fire; the host will not accept a second bakery wearing a fake mustache.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts a new place only when its ordinary function directly controls, stops, supplies, replaces, or undoes the previous place’s function; ignoring it, outlasting it, making it larger, or naming a neighboring place without a real counter loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one circus-town place and its practical action: "I am the fire station, spraying down the burning ticket booth."
sketches.first_card: The ticket booth is taking everyone’s money.
